newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan to export up to 2,500 bpd crude from April.
newsitem.headline: Sudan to export up to 2,500 bpd crude from April.

text.p: Sudan will start exporting crude oil for the first time in April at a rate of one cargo every fortnight or up to 2,500 barrels a day (bpd), the official news agency SUNA said on Wednesday.

The oil will be from the Adar Yel fields near Melut in Upper Nile state, which are operated by the Qatari-based company Gulf Petroleum (Sudan), and the customer is a German company which the agency did not name.

The agency quoted the deputy executive director of Gulf Petroleum, Abdulaziz Mubarak al-Dulaimi, as saying the company decided to export because the Adar Yel crude does not meet the specifications of the oil refinery at Port Sudan.
Another motive is to introduce the crude to the world and attract more oil firms to invest in Sudan, he added.

He said the Adar Yel fields were now producing 2,500 bpd of low sulphur oil. The fields have a production capacity of 5,000 bpd and Dulaimi said he expected production there to reach 10,000 bpd by the end of the year.
To raise production to 5,000 bpd, the company needs to buy more trucks to carry the crude from the White Nile river port of Rabak to Port Sudan, a distance of over 800 km (500 miles).
Dulaimi said his company had trucked 15,000 barrels to Port Sudan since production in Adar Yel started last month.

The company plans to sign agreements with sub-contractors to dig more wells in the field and by the end of this month the company and the Sudanese government will sign an agreement on production sharing, he added.
The Adar Yel fields are just on the southern side of the line between the north and southern Sudan, where southern rebels have been fighting for more autonomy since 1983.

The rebels and their allies in the northern opposition have said they consider oil companies working in Sudan legitimate military targets because their activities strengthen the Islamist government of President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.

Apart from Gulf Petroleum, the main foreign oil company operating in Sudan is the Canadian company Arakis Energy Corp. This month Arakis and its Chinese and Malaysian partners signed final agreements for a $1 billion project to develop three blocks west of Melut. The deal is for 25 years.
